If you go to the track and didn't learn something, you did it wrong.

And, it's really, really frustrating. Yes, I'm well aware that you are probably of the opinion that you can get out there and do it. After all, it's just driving a car! Never, in the history of ever, has anyone driven on a track for the first time and said, "Hey, that's exactly what I expected! It was easy!"

So, I'd love to tell you 'bout it - but it's a lot of info. Like, people spend entire lives trying to master this - and don't. They write entire books on the subject.

And, so, I'm not actually sure where to begin and there are so many different aspects of automobiles that one might be passionate about. There's a guy that collects internal Saab corporation documentation. There's a guy that loves old wheels, hubcaps, etc... There's a guy (or lady) that likes rat rods, hot rods, street rods, etc... There's people who like truck pulls, car shows, etc...

My passion is probably doing the best possible lap I can. I don't actually like racing other people very much. When there are other people on the track, you're just going to end up getting in the way of each other doing the perfect lap. I don't care if it's just six of you on the track. Given enough time, the odds of some of you smashing into one another approaches 100%!

Alas, empty tracks are REALLY fucking expensive. They kinda want you to staff 'em with things like recovery crews and emergency medical staff, as well as the folks who maintain it.

So, your best way is to join a private club that has track days and is sometimes invited to be a support race at reasonable fees. They've already got the staff on-hand and all the volunteers that make motorsport possible. Driving schools are also fairly inexpensive, but deserve many paragraphs of text.

That's right, you don't even have to pay a whole lot of money. You can volunteer and have the second best seat in the house.

What do you want to know about? What do you think it's like? Have you ever tried it? Where do you want to start? What expectations do you have? Where the hell am I supposed to begin? What do you already know?

And, I don't see this 'series' going on for very long. I'm not bringing my car back to another event like this last one. I won't be doing many (any?) more track days until next year. It's just too frustrating and I really, really like my car too much to do this to it.
